evidence: CAP-03.S05.T03-R01-F02 is closed by reading target, dependency registration, all open causes and durable changes, replacements, and reusable-input freshness in one coherent SQLite snapshot, then re-reading and comparing that complete authority under the queue's BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction before inserting a runnable job. Any intervening target, cause, change, dependency, replacement, or reusable-input change fails with no queue write.

CAP-03.S05.T03-R01-F01 is closed by a recalculation-specific worker event and live lease, exact plan fingerprint, exact target/provenance/dependency transformation, checkpoint requirement, and one SQLite transaction that appends N+1, stages its canonical output identity, and commits the workflow output/provenance. A missing, unfinished, cancelled, or recovered workflow, generic event, or substituted input cannot create a revision; exact replay returns the same candidate and output receipt.

CAP-03.S05.T03-R01-F03 is closed by checking prior-revision freshness inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE aggregate transaction used for restoration. The selected safe contract denies any prior revision with an open stale cause, so a human cannot turn obsolete dependency authority into a false-fresh adjudicated current revision. A fresh adjudicated prior still restores by appending N+2 with exact dependency/provenance/history retention.

The real-SQLite suite proves source replacement and stale propagation, exact selective plan construction, restart/replay, injected second-change admission denial with zero jobs, atomic candidate/workflow success, exact comparison, history retention, fresh human restoration, and stale restoration denial.

Adversarial cases prove no canonical write for missing, claimed-but-unstarted, cancelled, recovered-but-unfinished, generic-event, superseded-dependency, mismatched-plan, or stale-restore authority. Existing workflow cancellation/retry/recovery and dependency graph/repository suites remain green.

The application service depends on a stable atomic selective-recalculation repository contract; the SQLite adapter owns cross-table transaction mechanics while the aggregate UnitOfWork exposes only a narrow same-transaction freshness assertion. Workflow/storage documentation and the frozen Windows package inventory changed with those boundaries.

No schema migration, HTTP/renderer surface, governed experience reference, cloud service, destructive operation, automatic adjudication, or unrelated product authority changed. Historical revisions and adverse stale causes remain immutable.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: R01 exposed three coupled transaction-authority defects across workflow admission, canonical output commit, and human restoration. R02 therefore replays each at the narrowest real boundary: injected SQLite propagation at admission; exact live worker/plan/dependency/output binding in one candidate-and-completion transaction; and same-transaction stale denial for restore. Existing workflow contracts, queue recovery/cancellation, dependency graph, repository behavior, static quality, architecture, and a real frozen Windows build cover credible regression surfaces. No route, credential, dependency version, security policy, schema, renderer, or toolchain changed, so unrelated full service/security/UI/deployment suites remain deferred to the slice and W1 gates.

The complete foundation, service, e2e-local, security, data, graph, packaging, performance, recovery, and Windows x64 qualification matrix remains mandatory once at W1 exit.

reviewerDisposition.rootCauseAnalysis: R01 treated correct data selection, queue admission, aggregate append, and restore as individually guarded operations but did not model the transaction boundaries joining them. That allowed authority to change between planning and enqueue, permitted candidate creation without consumption of a successful exact workflow, and separated stale-state authority from restoration. R02 makes each cross-table invariant explicit at its mutation point: coherent plan snapshot plus admission CAS, atomic candidate/output completion, and transactional stale-restore denial.
